title: Dr. Avi Loeb's "UAP Science Advisory Council" has Same Government Status as Rocker Tom De Longe's "To The Stars."
excerpt: A skeptical blog about UFO claims, aliens, etc.
content:
So, we have been wondering what, exactly, is the status of Dr. Avi Loeb's so-called 'UAP Science Advisory Council'? Well, apparently it's one of several groups that  "advise" the intelligence community about UFOs (UAPs), but arre not sponsored by the government. 

Aaron Lukas is the Deputy Director of National Intelligence. He recently posted the following on X: 

 

So Dr. Loeb's  UAP Science Advisory Council is one of several such groups, and some of them are, frankly, rather loopy. In the Disclosure Foundation, we find many of the usual suspects, among them:

  • Christopher K. Mellon, formerly of Tom DeLonge's "To The Stars".
  • Astrophysicist Dr. Eric Davis, who claimed that a poltergeist followed him home from the Skinwalker Ranch. 
  • Dr. Avi Loeb, naturally.
  • Physicist Dr. Harold Puthoff, who tested Uri Geller's magic powers back in the 1970s, and found them to be genuine.

As well as an assortment of big movers and shakers who can undoubtedly sniff that there is money to be made in "Disclosure."

But we know all about "To The Stars" academy, having been following it from its start, and visiting its "Flagship Retail Store" several times.

TTSA's "Flagship Retail Store," Encinitas, CA, during its heyday.

Rocker Tom DeLonge (left) of Blink-182, and founder of TTSA.
               
DeLonge writes a children's' book about nudity, sold at his Flagship Retail Store.

              
A model of the spaceship that TTSA proposed to get us "To The Stars".
                     

 Tom DeLonge knows a lot about aliens. Dude, where's my saucer?

But all good things must come to an end. Around New Year's Day of 2021, TTSA seemed to be unraveling. Suddenly no more was heard from Mr. DeLonge, whose "Flagship Retail" store had suddenly closed without explanation.

So far as I am aware, Tom DeLonge is no longer associated with To The Stars, although he created it and hired the likes of Elizondo, Mellon, Puthoff, Semivan, etc. 

Good night!
